correctness.rationale: The nested case is the smaller ball, with no contact with the larger sphere except at internal tangency (where the larger-sphere contact is e₁). In proper overlap the concave squared-distance quadratics determine containment and actual contact sets. The pole prescription makes the smaller-sphere equality set s=−1/d, and the larger quadratic has its clipped vertex at s=1 exactly when (d²q²−1)h≤d²−1. The h map increases from 1−q to 1+q, giving the stated cutoff and retaining the singleton at equality. In the two-latitude branch the negative-square identities place the vertices at t and −1/(dt), both strictly interior to the normalized axis interval. Upon setting z=dt², the derivative of the squared separation has the negative sign of the positive factor in RESULT.md lines 114–121. The separation tends to 1+q at the lower t endpoint and equals Lc at t=1, where h=1+θ and the formulas agree. The two-contact probability measure has axial mean zero and second moment −s₊s₋=1/d, and uniform transverse second moment gives I_d/d (in d=2, equal weights on each two-point latitude). John's sufficient contact criterion therefore establishes unrestricted optimality and uniqueness.
